payload.label: Check pages at every width and device setting
payload.job: Open each page I give at every width and device setting and read every piece of text a person can see, refusing text that cannot be read, is drawn in a font the page did not ask for, is cut off or makes a phone scroll sideways
payload.description: Opens each of screens (each { id, html, route?, fonts?, ready?, steps?, widths?, modes? }) in a headless Chromium through Playwright (headless-browser/launch.mjs, with its quiet switches and one-browser-at-a-time admission), at every width of views.json (phone 390x844 with no sideways scroll, tablet, desktop) and in every mode (light, dark, forced colours, Dark Reader), or the widths and modes asked for, through runMatrix (check-screens.mjs). The page's HTML is answered by the browser itself at its route on a made-up origin; any other request the page makes is aborted, never sent. Each view is scrolled window by window and every visible text node is judged: contrast under WCAG AA against the colour really behind it, a glyph drawn by a platform font the screen does not declare in fonts (system names such as system-ui never count), text cut off or outside the window, a phone page wider than its window, and a control with no accessible name; a screen that does not open is a failure. allowlist (allowlist.json's shape, none when left out) drops a proven false positive or keeps a decided look as reported. Answers passed, failures ({ screen, width, mode, probe, selector, text, detail }), reported, counts (failures per probe) and report (views read, texts read, seconds per phase). Writes no file and keeps nothing; needs a Chromium Playwright can find. Refuses a screen without an id or html, two screens at one route, and a width or mode views.json does not name. The deploy check also opens a live origin or a Worker, takes pictures of failures, runs the real Dark Reader extension and refuses a deploy; this run checks only the pages given.

provenance.source: Trillion-X/trillion tools/check-every-screen-at-every-width/check-screens.mjs, in-page.mjs, views.json, allowlist.json and vendor/darkreader.js, moved in a9ee258 (#76); old capability row capabilities.json:558 at 4ffa1dc4a2^ (open every screen at every width and device setting and read every piece of text a person can see, before going live). check-given-pages.mjs is new: it serves the given pages inside the browser and runs runMatrix over them.

payload.label: Check live screens on a phone and a computer
payload.job: Open each live page at its real address the way a person's phone and computer open it, and measure how long it takes to first show, to be usable, its longest task, its console errors and failed requests; tap the controls named and say whether each did what it expects; keep a picture of each screen in the person's Files
payload.description: Opens each of pages (each { id, url, old_url?, reach?, ready?, taps? }) in a headless Chromium through Playwright (headless-browser/launch.mjs, with its quiet switches and one-browser-at-a-time admission) at each view of views.json (phone 390x844, tablet, desktop; all when left out, or the views asked for). Each view is a cold load in its own browser context. The phone has its CPU and network slowed as live-screens.json names (DATA); the desktop has none. For each page and view it answers: status, first_paint_ms, first_contentful_paint_ms, usable_ms (the ready selector is visible and the main thread has been idle for usable_idle_ms), blank_ms (until the screen first shows any text, picture or control), longest_task_ms, console_errors, failed_requests, and picture (the full screen as PNG, kept in the person's Files under /live-screens/<run>/ and returned by its 1f: identity; a picture the Files right cannot keep is returned as base64 when small). The same for old_url when given. taps are made on the new side after its load, one after another; each reports worked, ms, detail and a picture. It judges nothing: the caller compares the numbers with its own bar. It holds no key and signs nobody in: a signed-in screen is measured by tool:check-live-screens-signed-in. reach steps (taps and waits) run after load; the screen's usable time is then measured from the last reach tap, and load_usable_ms keeps the time from the page's load. A URL in the answer has its query removed. A view not begun by until is answered as skipped. Refuses a page without an id or url, a non-http address, a view views.json does not name, and an expect with no known key.

ready.description: A CSS selector that must be visible before the page is usable

until.description: Epoch milliseconds; a view not begun by then is answered as skipped

payload.label: Read when the proof account's sign-in ends
payload.job: Say, for each site the proof account is signed in to, when its sign-in ends and how many days are left, so it is minted again before the signed-in live check stops working
payload.description: Reads the vault's proof-sessions (JSON keyed by origin, mounted on descriptor 4) and answers, for each origin, when its sign-in ends: expires_at (ISO, UTC), the latest end of its cookies (the session cookie outlives the short cache cookies the server issues again), and days_left (one decimal), with each cookie's name and its own expires_at; a cookie with no end counts as none (null). It also answers renew: true when an account of proof-accounts.json has no session, or one that ends within its renew_when_days_left (the refresh workflow mints again only then). It answers names and times only: no cookie value is ever in the answer. The refresh workflow reads it daily and mints the session again before it ends.

provenance.source: group 9: held-session.mjs heldSessionExpiries, for the proof session's refresh workflow (tools/check-every-screen-at-every-width).

payload.label: Ask each site to send its proof account a sign-in code
payload.job: Ask each site the signed-in live check uses to email its proof account a one-time sign-in code, so the proof session can be minted again
payload.description: Step 1 of workflow:keep-the-proof-sessions-signed-in. For each proof account of proof-accounts.json (DATA: an origin and a test address whose mail reaches an AgentMail proof inbox), posts the site's better-auth send-verification-otp for that address. It holds no key and asks only for the addresses proof-accounts.json names. Answers asked_at (epoch ms, for step 2) and each origin's sent and status; refuses when no site sent a code.

origins.description: The proof accounts' origins to work on; all of proof-accounts.json when left out

provenance.source: group 9: proof-session-mint.mjs, from main dude's hand path mint-proof-sessions.mjs (Nov 21 2026), split in three runs by the key-host rule.

payload.label: Keep the proof accounts' sign-in codes in the vault
payload.job: Read each proof account's newest sign-in code from its proof inbox and keep the codes in the vault, never in an answer
payload.description: Step 2 of workflow:keep-the-proof-sessions-signed-in. With the vault's agentmail-api-key mounted on descriptor 4 (it reaches only the mailbox), reads each proof account's newest sign-in code sent after asked_at (email-code.mjs latestSignInCode, polled up to 30 s), and puts the codes as the vault value proof-sign-in-code (JSON keyed by origin), with the accounts' hosts, through the records door's secrets:put that its row names. Answers the origins kept and those whose code did not come; never a code.

origins.description: The proof accounts' origins to work on; all of proof-accounts.json when left out

payload.label: Sign the proof accounts in with their kept codes
payload.job: Exchange each kept sign-in code for its proof account's session at its site, check the session is that account's, and keep the sessions in the vault for the signed-in live check
payload.description: Step 3 of workflow:keep-the-proof-sessions-signed-in. With proof-sign-in-code on descriptor 4 and proof-sessions on descriptor 5 (both bound to the sites' hosts, so the run reaches only the sites), posts each code to the site's better-auth sign-in/email-otp, keeps the Set-Cookie session only when the site's get-session answers the proof account's address, puts the merged sessions as proof-sessions with the accounts' hosts, and marks proof-sign-in-code spent ({}). Answers each origin's signed_in, its cookies' names and ends, and its expires_at; never a code or a cookie value.
